extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators and researchers who submitted an NSF proposal (NSF proposal authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for PIs whose NSF proposals were not awarded, explaining how to use reviewer comments, revise substantially per PAPPG, consider program fit, consult program officers, and resubmit successfully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use reviewers' comments as a gift to improve your proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Every unfunded proposal notice sent to the PI comes with the reviewers’ comments attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These critiques contain invaluable advice and commentary on the intellectual merits and broader impacts displayed in your narrative, the strength of your research plan, and the expertise of your research team. If you believe your submission is a solid research proposal, treat the reviews as actionable feedback to guide revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmit only after substantial revision (PAPPG requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A declined proposal may be resubmitted, but only after it has undergone substantial revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per the PAPPG: 'A resubmitted proposal that has not clearly taken into account the major comments or concerns resulting from the prior NSF review may be returned without review.' The Foundation will treat the revised proposal as a new proposal, subject to standard review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clearly address major reviewer comments in the revision
rubrics_metrics.description: A resubmitted proposal must clearly take into account the major comments or concerns resulting from the prior NSF review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program officer expects you to demonstrate that you are open to constructive criticism and anxious to improve on your proposal. Failure to visibly respond to major critiques risks the submission being returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsider program/division fit if reviewers signal mismatch
rubrics_metrics.description: Use reviewers' comments to reconsider what division you pursue funding from.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sometimes reviewers indicate they don’t see a strong match between your research proposal and the opportunity you responded to. Comments about poor fit should prompt investigation of other NSF RFPs or divisions that better align with your research focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gather your team to collectively analyze and incorporate reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather your team together and go over the reviews together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brainstorm about how you can incorporate the comments into your work and strengthen the next proposal. Collaborative review helps identify technical weaknesses, clarify responsibilities, and generate stronger revision strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study awarded proposals to learn what NSF funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at the proposals that the NSF did award for the opportunity you applied to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Advanced feature of the NSF’s Awards page to filter by program and read abstracts of awarded proposals to get a deeper sense of what the NSF is looking for when making funding decisions. This can inform framing, emphasis, and scope in your revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact the program officer to discuss the declined notice
rubrics_metrics.description: You are encouraged by the NSF to contact the program officer and discuss the declined funding notice with that person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PO's email is on the notice. They can help you interpret reviewers' comments and possibly point you toward a different, more promising direction or program for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect persistence and multiple submissions per award
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF statistics show that on average, Principal Investigators submit about 2.3 proposals for every award they receive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many successful PIs have also been declined; treat declined notices as part of the process. Keep refining your research idea and keep submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared for multi-month review cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: The NSF takes about 5 to 6 months to review proposals and decide on awards for each opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow for this timeline when planning revisions and resubmissions; expect to wait several months for an outcome and plan next steps accordingly.
